column1: # Korean grammar words, endings and particles. One line per word as written + part of speech:
# word <TAB> UD part of speech <TAB> senses separated by " | ".
# The file replaces Wiktionary's determiner, pronoun, conjunction, particle and
# auxiliary entries for every word listed here; content words stay, and a line
# with a content part of speech comes before Wiktionary's of that part of speech.
# Particles and endings are written as Wiktionary writes them, with hyphens
# (-이나, -었-): the analyzer (`context.analyzer` in language.toml) gives each
# morpheme its base form spelled so (`baseSpellings`), and finds its line by it.
# A form after a `/` finds the same line (-으려면 for -려면).
# Lines are for what Wiktionary lacks or explains only by naming a form.
# Each sense explains what the word does, for a learner reading it next to
# the sentence: what it expresses, then the English, then a short phrase in
# brackets when the English alone doesn't settle it ("..., you see: politely
# explains or gives the reason: I was busy, you see (바빴거든요)"). No notes
# on position: the sentence shows those.
# Wiktionary lists 저 "that" before 저 "I", and 제 and 내 only as allomorphs:
# 저는 and 제가 opened on "that, that thing".

column3: I, me, lowering yourself politely: I'm a student (저는 학생이에요) | that, far from both of you: what's that? (저게 뭐예요?)
that, far from both of you: that person (저 사람)
I: 저 before -가: I'll do it (제가 할게요) → 저 | my, said politely: my name (제 이름)
I: 나 before -가: I'll do it (내가 할게) → 나 | my: my friend (내 친구)

or: photos or videos (사진이나 영상) | ... or something, offering loosely: shall we have coffee or something? (커피나 마실까요?) | as many as, more than expected: a whole three hours (세 시간이나) | just, for lack of anything better
called, as: names what comes before, with 하다 or 부르다: this is called kimchi (이것을 김치라 한다) | because it is: I'm busy because I'm a student (학생이라 바빠요)
called, said to be: quotes what a noun is: can be called an advantage (장점이라고 할 수 있다), he said it was a friend (친구라고 했다) | closes a direct quote: he said "let's go" ("가자"라고 했다)
called, named: a novel called Demian (데미안이라는 소설) | that is, linking a noun to the noun it describes: the fact that it is true (사실이라는 것)
as for, what we call: names a topic to define it: what is happiness? (행복이란 무엇인가)
if it is: if it's true (사실이라면), if I were you (나라면)
by means of, through: by providing (제공함으로써), through dialogue (대화로써)
from a person, place or source: from a friend (친구로부터)
or, such as: lists examples: apples or pears and such (사과라든가 배라든가)
as, following: as you said (말대로), as one pleases (마음대로), in order (순서대로)
and, so: sets the scene for what follows: it's raining and I have no umbrella (비가 오는데 우산이 없어요) | but, whereas: it's small but heavy (작은데 무거워요)
..., though; well, ...: politely sets out a situation and waits for a reply, or softens it: it's good, actually (좋은데요)
only if: you only know if you go (가야 알 수 있다) | with 하다 or 되다, must, have to: I have to go (가야 해요)
-아야 after a verb ending in 아: only if; with 하다, must: I have to go (가야 해요) → -아야 | calls someone by a name ending in a vowel: Minsu! (민수야)
I should, I'll have to, deciding it for yourself: I'll have to see (봐야겠어요)
if you want to, to do it: the aim a condition is for: if you want to go (가려면)
(formal) in order to, intending to: I would like to tell you (말씀드리고자 합니다)
if, supposing: if you go (간다면), if it's good (좋다면)
if, when: a spoken -면: if you turn it (돌리면은) → -면
that, quoting a statement to describe the noun after it: the news that he's coming (온다는 소식)
oh, ...!: politely says what you've just noticed or feel: it's tasty! (맛있네요)
..., you see: politely explains or gives the reason: I was busy, you see (바빴거든요)
I found that ...: politely reports what you saw or felt yourself: it was tasty, I found (맛있더라고요)
..., you know: politely reminds the listener of something they know or should agree with: it's cold, isn't it (춥잖아요)
...?: a gentle polite question: is it all right? (괜찮나요?)
shall I, shall we ...?: shall we go? (갈까요?) | do you think ...?, wondering: would there be? (있을까요?)
as, as you can see or know: as you know (아시다시피)
while, doing two things at once: I study while listening to music (음악을 들으면서 공부해요) | even though: pretends not to know though he knows (알면서 모른 척한다)
and, linking actions or descriptions, mostly in writing: is tall and strong (키가 크며 힘이 세다) | while: said with a smile (웃으며 말했다)

that, quoting what someone said: he said he would go (간다고 했다) | ..., they say: passes on what you heard: it's going to rain, they say (비가 온다고) | saying that, giving someone's reason: didn't come, saying he was busy (바쁘다고 안 왔다)

-ly, making an adverb: quickly (빠르게), loudly (크게) | so that: so that it can be seen well (잘 보이게) | with 되다, come to, end up: to come to know (알게 되다) | with 하다, make or let someone: to make someone laugh (웃게 하다) | in speech, I will ...: I'll do it (내가 하게)
so ...!, something just realized: so you're here already (벌써 왔구먼)
if one is to, to do it: so to speak (말하자면)
as for why or what ...: raises a question you then answer: because (왜냐면), the thing is (뭐냐면)
that means to, that is about to: a person who means to go (가려는 사람)
and then, after doing it: he went out after eating (밥을 먹고서 나갔다)

column1: ## Constructions over several words, a space apart
-을 수 있다/-ㄹ 수 있다/-을 수가 있다/-ㄹ 수가 있다/-을 수도 있다/-ㄹ 수도 있다
column3: can, be able to: I can go (갈 수 있다) | may, might: it may rain (비가 올 수 있다)

column1: -을 수 없다/-ㄹ 수 없다/-을 수가 없다/-ㄹ 수가 없다
column3: cannot: I can't believe it (믿을 수 없다)
have no choice but to: we have no choice but to wait (기다릴 수밖에 없다)
it will probably ..., so or but: an expectation: it'll probably rain, so ... (비가 올 텐데)
become, get, after an adjective: to get better (좋아지다) | be done, after a verb; 지다 makes it passive: to be made (만들어지다) → 지다
is doing it now: is eating (먹고 있다) | is in that state: is wearing (입고 있다)
after doing it, and then: after eating (먹고 나서)
want to: I want to go (가고 싶다)
not: doesn't go (가지 않다), isn't big (크지 않다)
can't, fail to, though you tried or wanted: couldn't sleep (자지 못했다)
come to, end up, how things turned out: to come to know (알게 되다)
make or let someone do it: to make someone laugh (웃게 하다)
because: because it rains (비가 오기 때문에)
have done it before: I have been there (가 본 적이 있다)
(spoken) and then, having done it: bought it and came (사 가지고 왔다) | so, because: because I was late (늦어 가지고)
according to, depending on: according to the rules (규칙에 따라), depending on the person (사람에 따라)
according to a source: according to the news (뉴스에 따르면)
about, regarding: about that problem (그 문제에 대해)
about, before a noun: a book about history (역사에 대한 책)
through, by way of: through the internet (인터넷을 통해)
centred on, around: centred on Seoul (서울을 중심으로)
by, naming who did it: was made by people (사람에 의해 만들어졌다) | owing to, due to
not only ... but also: not only Korea but also Japan (한국뿐만 아니라 일본도)
for example
besides this, in addition, apart from that
in a way, from one point of view
as it turned out, it turned out that
after that, then, next
to come to mind, to remember: I remembered that person (그 사람이 생각이 났다)
to influence, to affect: to affect one's health (건강에 영향을 주다)
-ic, -al: makes a describing word of a noun, with 인 or 으로: chemical (화학적), natural (자연적인), efficiently (효율적으로)
a respectful ending for people: teacher (선생님), dear customer (고객님)
type, model, form: the latest model (최신형)
rate, ratio: growth rate (성장률)
world, circle, field: academia (학계), ecosystem (생태계) | system: nervous system (신경계)
in terms of, as far as it goes: in history (역사상), legally (법률상)
sphere, zone: the capital region (수도권) | right: the right to vote (투표권) | ticket: admission ticket (입장권)
system: presidential system (대통령제) | medicine: digestive medicine (소화제)
group of people: the elderly (노년층) | layer: stratum (지층)
per: per person (1인당), per hour (시간당)
power, ability: competitiveness (경쟁력), influence (영향력)
feeling, sense of: sense of responsibility (책임감), confidence (자신감)
student: university student (대학생) | born in a year: born in 1990 (90년생)
by, sorted by: by age (연령별), by region (지역별)
around, about a time: around three o'clock (3시경)

column1: ## Bound nouns and adverbs whose common use Wiktionary lacks

column3: place | situation, case | for, in doing it: it takes an hour to get there (가는 데 한 시간 걸려요) | thing, what: turns what comes before it into a noun
together | like, as: like this (이와 같이), white as snow (눈같이 희다)
also | again | 또 다른: another: another problem (또 다른 문제)
once, one time | just try it, with a verb: give it a try (한번 해 보세요) | sometime, when there's a chance
not very, not much, with a negative: it's not that good (별로 안 좋아요)
less | not fully, not yet: not fully ripe (덜 익은)
in all, in total: twelve people in all (총 12명)
as, the way something is done: the way one does (하는 대로), as I saw (본 대로)
what: what are you doing? (뭐 해요?) | something: do you want something to eat? (뭐 먹을래?) | well, like: a filler: stuff like that (뭐 그런 거)
something: something is odd (뭔가 이상해요) | somehow, kind of
uh, um: hesitating | oh!, in surprise | (casual) yeah
ah, oh | uh, um: hesitating
now, from now on | so, well, and then: a filler (이제 뭐)
just, just now: I just arrived (막 도착했어요) | carelessly, any old way: eat anything (막 먹다) | like, you know: a filler
a little: short for 조금 → 조금 | please: softens a request: please help me (좀 도와주세요)
(casual) very, really: it's really good (되게 좋아요)
so, that's why | I mean, that is: what I mean is (그러니까 제 말은)
then, in that case | (그럼) of course, sure
still, even so, nevertheless
this, this thing: a spoken 이거 → 이거
this, this thing, as the subject: a spoken 이게 → 이게
this kind of: a spoken 이런 → 이런
like this: a spoken 이렇게 → 이렇게
